DEBT OBLIGATIONS ​ Long-term debt consists of: ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ January 31, ​ February 1, ​ ​ ​ ​ 2026 ​ ​ ​ 2025 1.70 % to 8.00 % Senior Notes due through 2064 ​ $ 14,864 ​ $ 14,854 Other ​ 1,011 ​ 1,055 ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Total debt, excluding obligations under finance leases ​ 15,875 ​ 15,909 Less current portion ​ ( 1,366 ) ​ ( 104 ) ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ Total long-term debt, excluding obligations under finance leases ​ $ 14,509 ​ $ 15,805 ​ In 2024, the Company issued $ 10,500 of senior notes to pay a portion of the cash consideration for its proposed merger with Albertsons and general corporate purposes. The Company repaid certain senior notes of $ 4,700 that were subject to a special mandatory redemption due to the termination of the merger. See Note 18 for additional information related to these issuances and repayments. ​ On September 13, 2024, the Company entered into an unsecured revolving credit facility (the “Credit Agreement”), with a termination date of September 13, 2029, unless extended as permitted under the Credit Agreement. The Credit Agreement amended the agreement governing the Company’s $ 2,750 credit facility that would otherwise have terminated on July 6, 2026. Under the Credit Agreement, the aggregate amount of initial commitments under the revolving credit facility is $ 2,750 , which could have been increased by $ 2,250 to $ 5,000 upon the closing date of the proposed merger with Albertsons (such additional commitments, the “Albertsons Closing Date Additional Commitments”). Concurrently with the termination of the merger agreement (the “Merger Agreement”) with Albertsons on December 11, 2024, the Albertsons Closing Date Additional Commitments were automatically terminated in accordance with the terms of the Credit Agreement. On and after December 11, 2024, the amount of outstanding commitments under the Credit Agreement is $ 2,750 . ​ Borrowings under the Credit Agreement bear interest, at the Company’s option, at either (i) adjusted Term Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) plus a market spread, based on the Company’s Public Debt Rating or (ii) the base rate, defined as the highest of (a) the Federal Funds Rate plus 0.5 %, (b) Wells Fargo’s prime rate , and (c) one month Term SOFR plus 1.0 %, plus a market rate spread based on the Company’s Public Debt Rating . The Company will also pay a Commitment Fee based on its Public Debt Rating and Letter of Credit fees equal to a market rate spread based on the Company’s Public Debt Rating. “Public Debt Rating” means, as of any date, the rating that has been most recently announced by either S&P or Moody’s, as the case may be, for any class of non-credit enhanced long-term senior unsecured debt issued by the Company. ​ The Credit Agreement contains a covenant, which, among other things, requires the maintenance of a leverage ratio of not greater than 3.50 :1.00. The Company may repay the Credit Agreement in whole or in part at any time without premium or penalty. The Credit Agreement is not guaranteed by the Company’s subsidiaries. ​

passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: RESULTS OF OPERATIONS. ​ The following discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations of The Kroger Co. should be read in conjunction with the “Forward-looking Statements” section set forth in Part I and the “Risk Factors” section set forth in Item 1A of Part I of this Annual Report on Form 10-K. MD&A is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying notes thereto contained in Item 8 of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, as well as Part II, Item 7 “Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended February 1, 2025, which provides additional information on comparisons of fiscal years 2024 and 2023. ​ OUR VALUE CREATION MODEL – DELIVERING CONSISTENT AND ATTRACTIVE TOTAL SHAREHOLDER RETURN ​ Kroger’s proven value creation model is allowing us to deliver today and invest for the future. The foundation of our value creation model is our omnichannel retail business, including fuel and health and wellness. By executing on our go-to-market strategy built on Fresh, Our Brands , Personalization and eCommerce, we are creating a shopping experience that builds loyalty and grows sales. Our retail business generates traffic and data which accelerates growth in our high operating margin alternative profit businesses, like retail media. In turn, the value generated from these businesses enables us to reinvest back into our retail business. ​ We are focused on our top priorities and delivering an exceptional customer experience to accelerate this flywheel effect. By expanding our store network and improving our eCommerce capabilities, we expect to grow households and increase sales. Our model provides various ways to generate net earnings growth. ​ We believe this will be achieved by: ​ ● Growing identical sales without fuel. Our plan involves maximizing growth opportunities in our retail business and is supported by continued strategic investments in our associates and greater value for our customers to ensure we deliver a full, fresh and friendly experience for every customer, every time. In an effort to serve more households, we plan to invest in major storing projects that allow us to increase both in-store and eCommerce sales. As more and more customers incorporate eCommerce into their permanent routines, we expect eCommerce sales to grow at a double-digit rate – a faster pace than other food at home sales – over time; and ​ ● Expanding operating margin through long-term initiatives in gross margin, growing alternative profit businesses and productivity and cost savings initiatives that are focused on simplifying our business and modernizing our ways of working. Together, we expect these will enable us to improve operating margin, while balancing strategic price investments for customers and investments in associates to improve customer experience. ​ We expect to continue to generate strong free cash flow and are committed to being disciplined with capital deployment in support of our value creation model and stated capital allocation priorities. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital spending, leaving meaningful free cash flow that can service fixed obligations and fund shareholder returns. Cash generation sits well above the sector median on a cash-flow-to-debt basis, and the indicative cash-flow tier is the strongest, giving the issuer a durable buffer against grocery margin volatility.

The debt stack is almost entirely long-dated senior notes, with only a modest current portion due in the next twelve months and the bulk maturing beyond five years. This laddered profile, plus an undrawn committed revolver maturing in the medium term, limits near-term refinancing pressure and preserves liquidity flexibility.

key_risks.text: Operating income fell sharply year over year, compressing operating margin to a low-single-digit level that sits far below the sector median. With thin grocery margins, even modest sales or cost pressure can erode EBITDA and push leverage toward the covenant threshold, leaving limited headroom before a downgrade trigger.

The debt note discloses a leverage covenant of not greater than three and a half times, tested under the revolver, and the facility is unguaranteed by subsidiaries. A material EBITDA decline or debt-funded action could breach this maintenance test, constraining liquidity access precisely when refinancing or merger-related funding needs arise.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is thin relative to the sector median, reflecting the heavy senior-note stack and elevated cash interest burden. Although operating cash flow covers interest many times over, the coverage ratio leaves little cushion if operating income remains at current depressed levels or if refinancing occurs at higher coupons.

Free cash flow covers only a modest share of total debt, and shareholder distributions absorb most of that free cash flow, leaving limited retained cash for deleveraging. With dividends and buybacks consuming the bulk of internally generated funds, debt reduction depends on EBITDA recovery rather than organic cash retention.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, with leverage modestly below the sector median but coverage and margin well below peer norms. The combination of weak operating profitability, a large long-dated debt stack and shareholder returns that absorb free cash flow argues for a cautious stance pending evidence of margin recovery.

Analyst judgement: the issuer retains adequate liquidity and a manageable maturity ladder, but the thin margin and covenant headroom mean credit quality is sensitive to grocery demand and cost trends. Deleveraging toward the upgrade threshold would require sustained EBITDA improvement or reduced shareholder distributions, neither of which is assured.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流穩健覆蓋資本開支，留下可觀的自由現金流，足以償付固定債務並支持股東回報。以現金流對債務比率計，現金生成能力遠高於行業中位數，而指示性現金流級別為最強，為發行人提供持久緩衝，抵禦雜貨利潤率波動。
債務結構幾乎全為長年期優先票據，僅有少量流動部分於未來十二個月內到期，大部分於五年後到期。此階梯式到期結構，加上中期到期的未提取承諾循環信貸，限制了近期再融資壓力並保持流動性靈活性。

key_risks.text: 營運收入按年大幅下降，營運利潤率壓縮至低單位數水平，遠低於行業中位數。雜貨利潤率微薄，即使銷售或成本壓力溫和，亦可能侵蝕 EBITDA 並推高槓桿至契約門檻，令降級觸發前的緩衝空間有限。
債務票據披露槓桿契約為不高於三倍半，於循環信貸下測試，且該融資未獲附屬公司擔保。EBITDA 大幅下降或債務融資行動可能違反此維持測試，在再融資或併購相關資金需求出現時，正好限制流動性獲取。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率相對行業中位數偏薄，反映沉重的優先票據結構及高企的現金利息負擔。儘管營運現金流覆蓋利息多倍，但若營運收入維持當前低迷水平或再融資以更高票息進行，覆蓋比率緩衝有限。
自由現金流僅覆蓋總債務的一小部分，而股東分派吸收大部分自由現金流，留下有限留存現金用於去槓桿。股息及回購消耗大部分內部產生資金，債務削減依賴 EBITDA 復甦而非內生現金留存。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為中等，槓桿略低於行業中位數，但覆蓋率及利潤率遠低於同業常規。營運盈利能力疲弱、龐大長年期債務結構及吸收自由現金流的股東回報，共同支持謹慎立場，待利潤率復甦證據出現。
分析師判斷：發行人保持充足流動性及可管理的到期階梯，但微薄利潤率及契約緩衝意味著信用質量對雜貨需求及成本趨勢敏感。去槓桿至升級門檻需持續 EBITDA 改善或減少股東分派，兩者均不保證。
